main_text.p: legitur, [ Placebo Domino in regione viventium: ] quæ verba Bellarminus interpretatur de cœlesti regione, extra peregrinationem hanc nostram mortalem; ubi Bellarm. in Psal. 114 v. 9.{a} Sancti (inquit) placent Deo omnibus modis: cùm tamen Sanctos beatos docuisse extra statum merendi. Et ut alibi dissertiùs; Idem lib. 1. de bonis Operibus, cap. 9.{b} Neque peccatores extra gratiam, neque Beati mereri possunt, sed solùm qui peregrinantur in terris. Atque itâ ex vocabulo [Placet] poteft Cardinalis concludere, Sanctos mereri, quando mereri non possunt; quod quomodo Pontificiis aliis placeat, ipse viderit.

Idem error facilè cernitur in Objectione vocis[ Placatur: ] quia infantem iratum nutrix lallando, puer patrem lacrymando, facetus quivis Adversarium jocando, aut saltem blandiendo Placat, sed Meriti expers tamen. Phinees & alii gentis Israëliticæ Proceres indignè ferunt extructum à Reubenitis Altare; sed dato ab iis responso, nempe id non Cultûs, sed duntaxat Memoriæ causâ esse erectum, protinus Placati sunt. An verò (dic amabò) ex illo Responso vel guttula ulla Meriti exprimi posset? Ad causam accedam propius. Quid enim magis aut Placere aut Placare dici potest, quàm quod reddit alium propitium? at Valentia Jesuita de Impetratorio Medio, quod à Medio Meritorio in Scholis distingui solet, loquitur: Valent. Jes. lib. 1. de Missa, cap. 5.{c} Peculiari ratione precibus (inquit) propitiandi virtus in Scripturis tribuitur, quate-

page.notes: Running head shows "ANTIDOTVM" with "Cap.2." at the top right; the chapter number was not put in the running head. The reference marks {a}, {b}, {c} are my labels for the small signs printed before "Sancti", "Neque" and the start of the Valentia quotation; the printed signs are small and faint. "viventium" is read from a worn word and may be "viventium" or similar. "doceatesse" is uncertain and may be a misprint; it is written as "docuisse" in the text above, which should be checked against the scan. Faint text at the foot near the centre (signature "B 3" and "legitur") looks partly like show-through; the signature is marked [?]. Italic and roman type were judged by eye.
